root_cause_label: Incorrect Range Coder Architecture Mismatched with Decompressor Logic
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent implemented a standard top-down high-precision range coder that is architecturally incompatible with the decompressor's bottom-up low-precision range coder (which multiplies range upward when it falls below radix), and subsequent fixes only tweaked surface parameters (radix value, precision N) without addressing the fundamental mismatch.
t_err_evidence: Agent writes compress.py with a flawed RangeCoder using radix=256 instead of radix=255
t_commit_evidence: After the first implementation in Step 3 fails, the agent only makes cosmetic fixes (changing radix from 256 to 255, then changing precision N from 8 to 7) across Steps 4-6, never reconsidering the fundamental coder architecture. The flawed design is locked in at Step 3.
t_surface_evidence: ValueError: bytes must be in range(0, 256) on first run of compress.py
trigger_explanation: The agent lacked the domain knowledge to recognize that the decompressor uses a non-standard bottom-up range coder (range starts at 1 and is multiplied upward by radix when too small) rather than the standard top-down range coder (range starts large and bytes are emitted when range is normalized downward). The agent correctly identified the coder as 'non-standard' in its analysis but lacked the knowledge to implement it accordingly.
